questions.sample_criteria: Candidate should mention idempotency keys (UUIDs), distributed locks (Redis Redlock/database unique constraints), transaction statuses (INITIATED, SUCCESS, FAILED), and caching response payloads for identical keys.

questions.question: What are the core tradeoffs between Server-Side Rendering (SSR), Static Site Generation (SSG), and Incremental Static Regeneration (ISR)?
questions.sample_criteria: SSG gives fastest TTFB at build-time cost; SSR renders dynamic user-specific data per request with server latency; ISR periodically regenerates static pages in background on cache stale.

questions.question: How does the Java Garbage Collector handle circular object references between two unused objects in the heap?
questions.sample_criteria: Candidate should explain Tracing Garbage Collection (GC Roots, Mark and Sweep) rather than simple reference counting, clarifying that unreachable circular graphs are collected.

questions.question: Explain the difference between optimistic concurrency control and pessimistic locking in PostgreSQL. Under what transaction throughput conditions would you choose each?
questions.sample_criteria: Candidate should define OCC (version/timestamp checks) vs Pessimistic (SELECT FOR UPDATE locks), noting OCC works best in low-contention high-throughput scenarios, while pessimistic is safer in high-contention balance deductions.

questions.question: How does Python manage concurrency with the Global Interpreter Lock (GIL), and when should you use multiprocessing or asyncio instead of threading?
questions.sample_criteria: GIL ensures only one thread executes bytecode at a time. I/O-bound tasks benefit from threading/asyncio; CPU-bound tasks require multiprocessing to leverage multiple CPU cores.
